questions.knowledge_point: Integrating Functions Containing the Natural Logarithm
questions.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2x}\cdot 2=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}\,\text{d}x & =2\int \frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =2\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡|\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)|+C\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$

$$

Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2}).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}}\cdot 2x=\frac{2}{x}\,⟹\,\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})}{3x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{3}\int \operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2})\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x}\cdot  \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\int u\cdot (\frac{1}{2}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\int u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{6}\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{12}{u}^{2}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{12}{ln}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})+C\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{3}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x{log}_{3}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{log}_{3}⁡x}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\int \frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡|{log}_{3}⁡x|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{2}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{2}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & =\int {log}_{2}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\int u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\int u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot \frac{{log}_{2}^{2}⁡x}{2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{3}⁡(2x).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3}{x{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{3}{{log}_{3}⁡(2x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\int \frac{3}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡3\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡3\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡3\operatorname{ln}⁡|{log}_{3}⁡(2x)|+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2}).$Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,⟹\,\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})}{x}\,\text{d}x & =\int {log}_{3}⁡({x}^{2})\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\int u\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\,\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\int u\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3{log}_{3}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{2}⁡({x}^{2}).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,⟹\,\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{2}\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{{log}_{2}⁡({x}^{2})}{x}\,\text{d}x & =\int {log}_{2}⁡({x}^{2})\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\int u\cdot (\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{2}\text{d}u) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{2}\int u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2}{2}\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}+C \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡2{log}_{2}^{2}⁡({x}^{2})}{4}+C.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{4}^{32}\frac{1}{x\sqrt{{log}_{2}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x=($
{{field-1}}
$)\operatorname{ln}⁡2$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{2}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡2}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot \text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $4$ | $32$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $5$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{4}^{32}\frac{1}{x\sqrt{{log}_{2}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{4}^{32}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{log}_{2}⁡x}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & ={\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡2\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2{\int }_{2}^{5}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡2\cdot 2\sqrt{u}\,{|}_{2}^{5} \\  & =(2\sqrt{5}-2\sqrt{2})\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{3}^{81}\frac{2}{x\sqrt{{log}_{3}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x=($
{{field-1}}
$)\operatorname{ln}⁡3$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{3}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $3$ | $81$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{81}\frac{2}{x\sqrt{{log}_{3}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{3}^{81}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{log}_{3}⁡x}}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =2{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡3{\int }_{1}^{4}{u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot (2\sqrt{u}){|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡3(\sqrt{4}-\sqrt{1}) \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡3(2-1) \\  & =(4)\operatorname{ln}⁡3\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the following integral. Do not round the answer.

${\int }_{5}^{125}\frac{8}{3x{log}_{5}⁡({x}^{2})}\,\text{d}x=($
{{field-1}}
$)\,\operatorname{ln}⁡5$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{5}⁡({x}^{2}).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{{x}^{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\cdot 2x=\frac{2}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡5}\,⟹\,\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{2}\cdot \text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $5$ | $125$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $6$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{5}^{125}\frac{8}{3x{log}_{5}⁡({x}^{2})}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{8}{3}{\int }_{5}^{125}\frac{1}{{log}_{5}⁡({x}^{2})}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{8}{3}{\int }_{2}^{6}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{4\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{3}{\int }_{2}^{6}\frac{1}{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{4\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{2}^{6} \\  & =\frac{4\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡6-\operatorname{ln}⁡2) \\  & =\frac{4\operatorname{ln}⁡5}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡3 \\  & =(\frac{4}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡3)\operatorname{ln}⁡5\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{4x}\cdot 4=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $e/4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $\operatorname{ln}⁡4$ | $1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{e/4}\frac{1}{4x\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{1}^{e/4}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(4x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{1}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{\operatorname{ln}⁡4}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡4)) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}(0-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡4)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{ln}⁡(\operatorname{ln}⁡4)\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e$ | ${e}^{4}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{5\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{4x}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{5}{4}{\int }_{e}^{{e}^{4}}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{5}{4}{\int }_{1}^{4}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\frac{5}{4}\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{5}{8}\cdot {u}^{2}\,{|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =\frac{5}{8}({4}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{5}{8}\cdot 15 \\  & =\frac{75}{8}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Integrating Functions Containing the Natural Logarithm
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's set $u = \ln x.$ Then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= \dfrac 1 x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}u=\dfrac 1 x\,{\textrm{d}x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}\int \frac{3}{x\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}\,\text{d}x & =3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =3\int \frac{1}{\sqrt{u}}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\int {u}^{-1/2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =3\cdot 2{u}^{1/2}+C \\  & =6\sqrt{u}+C \\  & =6\sqrt{\operatorname{ln}⁡x}+C\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the integral $\displaystyle \int \dfrac{\log^2_3 x }{x} \,\textrm d x.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Let's rewrite our integral as

$$
\int \dfrac{(\log_3 x)^2 }{x} \,\textrm d x.
$$

Let $u=\log_3 x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d x} = \dfrac{1}{x\ln 3}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\ln 3\,\textrm d u = \dfrac 1 x \textrm d x.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}}{x}\,\text{d}x & =\int ({log}_{3}⁡x)^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int {u}^{2}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\int {u}^{2}\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \frac{1}{3}{u}^{3}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡3({log}_{3}⁡x)^{3}+C \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡3{log}_{3}^{3}⁡x+C\end{aligned}
$$

Let's set $u = \ln x.$ Then, we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}x}= \dfrac 1 x\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \textrm{d}u=\dfrac 1 x\,{\textrm{d}x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e$ | $e^2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\eqalign{
	\int_{e}^{e^2} \dfrac{\ln^2 x}{x}\,\textrm{d}x
&= \int_{e}^{e^2} (\ln x)^2\cdot \dfrac{\textrm{d}x}{x}\[5pt]
&=\int_{1}^{2} u^2\,\textrm{d}u\[5pt]
&=\left.\dfrac13u^{3}\right|_{1}^{2}\[5pt] 
&=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(2^3-1^3 \right)\[5pt]
&=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(8-1 \right)\[5pt]
&=\dfrac{7}{3}		

	}
$$
